speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This enables us to take into account business needs and ensure employees' employability.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think we have one of the lowest minimum number of annual leave entitlements in the world.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In this region, there is a whole list of countries – Malaysia, Myanmar, Mongolia, Laos, Indonesia – that actually provide a higher number of minimum days of annual leave and they provide a higher number of public holidays as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I really hope MOM can review this and study whether we can provide a higher number of minimum days of annual leave, also because I do believe that it is probably our lowest income workers who get these seven days.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Those are the workers that do the most backbreaking work that will need the rest.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If we do not increase it, it is likely that they just have the seven days.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Some, like the United Kingdom and Australia, have relatively more generous provisions while the United States does not have a federal law regulating paid annual leave.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Employees can use these other forms of leave over and above their annual leave entitlements.
